saipen_version.description: Protocol major version that wrote this state. Read from VERSION at checkpoint time.

schema_version.description: STATE file-format revision, integer. The current revision comes from this schema's x-current-schema-version metadata; revision 2 introduced the Core last_event checkpoint marker. Schema v1 or absence remains readable legacy and WARNs, then MUST upgrade at the next checkpoint. Deliberately NOT in `required`: listing it there would hard-fail exactly the legacy states tools/validate.py must still open. Distinct from `saipen_version`, which is the protocol MAJOR that wrote the state.

saipen_home.description: RFC § 1.7's bootloader pointer: absolute path to SAIPEN home on the machine that last checkpointed.

goal_waves.description: Safety-valve counter, RFC § 2.4. MUST be present when goal_mode: true, MUST be absent when goal_mode: false.

goal_tickets.description: Safety-valve counter, RFC § 2.4. MUST be present when goal_mode: true, MUST be absent when goal_mode: false.

last_event.description: Numeric N from the highest E-N event in the Core LOG at the checkpoint that produced this STATE. REQUIRED by tools/validate.py when schema_version is 2 and LOG contains an event; omitted only for a fresh empty LOG or readable legacy v1 state. Kept out of the JSON Schema `required` array because that array cannot express either condition.

human_note.description: Optional one-line human->agent nudge, read on continue (RFC § 1.2) and cleared once applied. Not a ticket, not a goal.

transition_from.description: The phase this state transitioned FROM. REQUIRED on every state except a fresh INIT -- part of RFC § 1.2's required set, which is the normative list; this file is its machine-readable mirror, never a second opinion about it. Deliberately NOT in `required`: that array cannot express 'except fresh INIT', and listing it there would hard-fail exactly the bootstrap state RFC § 1.2 exempts -- the same reason schema_version is kept out. The conditional is enforced in tools/validate.py instead (FAIL when phase is not INIT, WARN when it is), so absence from `required` here means 'checked elsewhere', never 'optional'. Combined with `phase` to validate transitions against RFC § 1.6. A fresh INIT bootstrap may set transition_from: INIT (self-referential, logically 'came from nothing').
